Ultragenyx reported Q3 2026 results: revenue $173.0M (missed $184.25M consensus by 6.1%); reaffirmed FY2026 Crysvita revenue guidance of $500M-$520M; cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $401M as of Sept 30, 2026

Announced a ~20% workforce reduction (to roughly 1,000 employees); wound down GTX-102 Angelman program and discontinued UX701 (Wilson disease gene therapy); ~$25M of Q4 2026 restructuring charges expected; reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $730-760M
Agreed to sell two priority review vouchers for $413M combined (~$350M expected net proceeds)

Full Q3 2026 figures confirmed via SEC 8-K exhibit: GAAP net loss $118M (-$1.16/share) vs $180M (-$1.81/share) in Q3 2025; nine-month 2026 net loss $395M (-$3.89/share). Revenue $173M (CRYSVITA $109M, DOJOLVI $30M per the exhibit breakdown) vs consensus near $183.5M-$185M. Pre-report non-GAAP consensus estimates found this session ranged from -$0.66 to -$0.88/share across sources (not directly comparable to the GAAP actual).

Ultragenyx reported Q3 2026 revenue of $173M, below analyst estimates of roughly $183.5M-$185.2M; announced substantial expense and headcount reductions expected to cut 2027 R&D spend by at least 50% vs. 2025, and reaffirmed its expectation to be profitable in 2027. Full Q3 EPS figure not found this session.

Ultragenyx's $210 million priority review voucher sale tied to the GENGLYCOS (gene therapy for GSDIa) accelerated approval closed in late October 2026; a second voucher sale (Fayuvi, $203M) was expected to close later in November 2026. Combined net proceeds from both vouchers were expected to total approximately $350 million.
catalysts.note: Exact close date approximated as 'late October 2026' per source wording; the Fayuvi voucher sale closing (expected later in Nov 2026) had not been confirmed as completed as of this research.

catalysts.headline: FDA granted full approval of FAYUVI (UX111, rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf) gene therapy, the first-ever approved treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA); Ultragenyx received a Priority Review Voucher
catalysts.impact: shares jumped ~12.6-13%, with further gains after-hours

catalysts.headline: Ultragenyx's Phase 3 ASPIRE study of apazunersen (GTX-102) in Angelman syndrome missed its primary endpoint (change from baseline in Bayley-4 cognitive raw score) and its key secondary endpoint (Multidomain Responder Index net response); safety was consistent with the earlier Phase 1/2 data. Company said it is evaluating the program's disposition and will implement 'significant' expense reductions.
catalysts.impact: Shares fell approximately 44-46% (reported variously, e.g. close of $14.84 vs prior close, down $11.68/-44%); JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral from Overweight and cut its price target to $36 from $80; Evercore cut its target to $16; this appears NOT to be reflected in the on-file market cap/EPS figures, which are dated Aug 20, 2026 (pre-crash) — see conflicts
